title: ～と言われている — it is said that ～
summary: Reports what people in general say or believe: “it is said that ～.” It attaches to the plain form of a sentence. It is used for general knowledge, tradition, legends and widely held opinions, and sounds a bit formal.

patterns.form: 普通形 ＋ と言われている／と言われています
patterns.gloss: plain form + と言われている (passive of 言う + ている)

body.p: 言われている is the passive of 言う plus ている, “is being said”. The source is not a particular person but people in general, so it is a good fit for facts that are widely known or handed down.
～と聞いた says that you personally heard it from someone. ～と言われている is a general report with no personal source. It is often used in explanations, news and guidebooks.

examples.ja: この寺（てら）は千年前（せんねんまえ）に建（た）てられたと言（い）われています。
examples.romaji: Kono tera wa sennen mae ni taterareta to iwarete imasu.
examples.tr: It is said that this temple was built a thousand years ago.

examples.ja: この果物（くだもの）は体（からだ）にいいと言（い）われている。
examples.romaji: Kono kudamono wa karada ni ii to iwarete iru.
examples.tr: This fruit is said to be good for your health.

examples.ja: その山（やま）には昔（むかし）神様（かみさま）がいたと言（い）われています。
examples.romaji: Sono yama ni wa mukashi kamisama ga ita to iwarete imasu.
examples.tr: It is said that long ago a god lived on that mountain.

pitfalls: Do not use it for something you heard from a specific person; use ～と聞いた or ～そうだ for that.
Keep ている: 言われる alone sounds like a one-time event of being told something.
